title: CDDP-EAGLE-1: DICOM converted whole slide images from the Environment And Genetics in Lung cancer Etiology (EAGLE) study
abstract: Abstract: The role of smoking has been well-documented in lung cancer for over 50 years. Less well-understood is why only 15-20 percent of smokers are afflicted with lung cancer and a small proportion of lung cancer occurs in the absence of smoking. A key goal of the EAGLE Study was to understand the role of inherited variation in smokers with lung cancer. This dataset corresponds to a collection of images and/or image-derived data available from the National Cancer Institute Imaging Data Commons (IDC). This dataset was converted into DICOM representation and ingested by the IDC team. You can explore and visualize the corresponding images using the IDC Portal. You can use the manifests included in this Zenodo record to download the collection following the Download instructions below. The Environment And Genetics in Lung cancer Etiology (EAGLE) study is a large, multicenter, population-based case-control study conducted in the Lombardy region of Italy from 2002 to 2005. The study enrolled over 2,000 incident lung cancer cases (ages 35-79) from 13 hospitals and over 2,000 matched population-based controls, to investigate the role of inherited genetic variation and environmental factors in lung cancer etiology. This collection contains DICOM converted whole slide images of H&E-stained (hematoxylin and eosin) frozen sections of primary lung tumor tissue from 49 of the 50 EAGLE lung adenocarcinoma cases available in the GDC CDDP_EAGLE-1 project (dbGaP accession phs001239). The original Aperio SVS slide images were converted to DICOM Slide Microscopy (SM) format using idc-wsi-conversion. Diagnoses include adenocarcinoma NOS (24 cases), adenocarcinoma with mixed subtypes (13), acinar cell carcinoma (8), clear cell adenocarcinoma (2), and solid carcinoma (2), coded in ICD-O-3. Data organization: DICOM PatientIDs correspond to GDC case IDs (e.g. CDDP_EAGLE-1-CDDP_00002) and can be used to link to genomic and clinical data in the GDC portal. Of 50 cases in GDC, 49 have Tissue Slide images; the remaining case has no slide and is not represented in this collection. The EAGLE study was led by Maria Teresa Landi, M.D., Ph.D. (NCI Division of Cancer Epidemiology and Genetics) in collaboration with EPOCA at the University of Milan. Please see the EAGLE Study page and the dbGaP study page to learn more about the study and to obtain any supporting metadata for this collection. Files included A manifest file's name indicates the IDC data release in which a version of collection data was first introduced. For example, cddp_eagle_1-idc_v22-aws.s5cmd corresponds to the contents of the cddp_eagle_1 collection introduced in IDC data release v22. cddp_eagle_1-idc_v25-aws.s5cmd: AWS download manifest cddp_eagle_1-idc_v25-gcs.s5cmd: GCS download manifest cddp_eagle_1-idc_v25-dcf.dcf: DCF download manifest Manifest files ending in -aws.s5cmd reference files in Amazon Web Services (AWS) buckets; -gcs.s5cmd reference files in Google Cloud Storage. The actual files are identical and mirrored between AWS and GCP. Download instructions Each manifest file includes instructions in its header on how to download the included files. To download the files using .s5cmd manifests: Install idc-index: pip install --upgrade idc-index Download the files referenced by a manifest included in this dataset: idc download manifest.s5cmd To download files using a .dcf manifest, see the manifest header. title: An Optimized Analytical Workflow for Magnetite as an Indicator Mineral for Porphyry Cu Deposits
abstract: Abstract Laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry is commonly used to measure trace element concentrations in magnetite, an indicator mineral that can serve as a geochemical vector to various types of ore deposits. Herein, we optimize the speed and efficiency of analytical workflows for discriminating hydrothermal ore-related magnetite grains in till samples. Four laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry workflows, varying in laser ablation time, calibration standards, and editing of the time-resolved signal, were evaluated for their ability to classify hydrothermal magnetite grains using a linear discriminant analysis model applied to till samples collected proximal to a porphyry Cu deposit. Calibration using Fe-poor NIST glass standards resulted in lower analytical accuracy in external standards than calibration using USGS basaltic glasses, indicating that higher-Fe basaltic glass standards provide a better calibration match for Fe-rich magnetite. Detailed inspection of the analytical data shows that a rapid workflow using only 10 s of laser ablation, 100 μm spot sizes, and no manual editing of the time-resolved signal produces nearly identical results for key classification elements (Fe, Mg, Al, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Co, Ni) and yields comparable hydrothermal magnetite classification to more time-consuming workflows. The rapid workflow also estimates the proportion of hydrothermal magnetite in a bulk till sample to within ±4% of results obtained using more time-consuming analytical approaches. Mean similarity coefficients of ∼0.95 between the most and least efficient workflows indicate that our optimized workflow provides a rapid and reliable method for exploration programs seeking to discriminate hydrothermal magnetite as an indicator mineral in till or stream sediment samples, while substantially reducing analytical and data-processing time.

title: Identification of concealed faults in the Changbaishan volcanic area based on the volcanic geomorphologic and soil gas geochemical surveys
abstract: 查明火山活动相关断裂的分布与位置，对火山监测具有重要意义。本文结合火山地质地貌特征，在长白山天池火山锦江温泉地热区开展了土壤气体地球化学观测，获取了研究区6条测线的土壤气体（CO2、Rn和H2）浓度背景及剖面分布特征。结果表明：靠近温泉区域，CO2浓度为0.31 %~75 %，H2浓度为1.03 ×10-6 ~347.80 ×10-6，Rn浓度为0.46 kBq·m-3~56.5 kBq·m-3；远离温泉群区域，CO2浓度为0.35 %~4.26 %，Rn浓度为12.10 kBq·m-3~50.10 kBq·m-3。6条剖面的气体浓度均呈现显著的单峰或紧凑型双峰空间变化特征。综合6条土壤气体剖面的气体空间分布特征及其他资料，认为研究区存在一条走向为NNW向的断裂，其走向与温泉点的分布方向一致。该NNW向断裂是进一步开展火山气体连续监测的理想区域。本文研究案例表明气体地球化学测量与火山地形地貌特征结合，可有效识别活动火山区隐伏断裂。

title: Pilot study of the knowledge graph and question-answering system for earthquake communication network operation and maintenance in Shaanxi Province
abstract: Facing challenges of multiple operation and maintenance entities, extensive materials, and multiple users, a question-answering system based on the knowledge graph of earthquake communication network operation and maintenance in Shaanxi Province has been established. The system utilizes Neo4j for knowledge storage, employs the Django framework for system development, and achieves the digitization and visualization of network operation knowledge and experience. A question-answering system based on retrieval-augmented generation was implemented based on this knowledge graph, providing accurate answers to users, effectively reduce time costs, and improve work efficiency.

title: Over-the-Horizon Radar Tracking of Multiple Aerial Targets under a Spherical Earth Approximation
abstract: Skywave Over-the-Horizon Radar can track multiple aerial targets far beyond the field of view of conventional line of sight radar. This paper presents a tracking algorithm tailored for skywave Over-the-Horizon Radar systems, utilizing Joint Probabilistic Data Association (JPDA) for tracking aerial targets. The proposed approach addresses the challenges of tracking in multi-target, multi-path propagation environment considering the simultaneous multi-path reflections from multiple ionospheric layers along with the line of sight path. A spherical earth approximation was considered to account for the curvature of the Earth. The tracking algorithm was tested with an Over-the-Horizon radar data generator using simulated scenarios. The tracker used a Gaussian model of the ionospheric heights for different transmission paths with different locations of transmitter, receiver and target trajectories. The results show good accuracy for tracking multiple simulated targets over the airspace of Europe.

title: FedGRAIL: Trustworthy and Efficient Federated Class-Incremental Learning for Long-Tailed IoT Edge Intelligence
abstract: In Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI) agents have become a core paradigm for edge intelligence, supporting on-device sensor data processing and privacy-preserving analytics. In practice, however, the sensor data streams evolve continuously and often exhibit nonindependent and identically distributed (non-IID) characteristics. Federated class-incremental learning (FCIL) has thus emerged as a promising approach to endow edge AI agents with long-tail learning capabilities, allowing models to adapt autonomously to persistent changes in the data. Despite recent progress, most existing FCIL methods assume balanced data distributions, which rarely hold in real-world deployments. Under realistic long-tailed distributions, the local optimization objectives of individual AI agents diverge from the desired global convergence, leading to head-class bias and rapid forgetting of tail classes. To overcome these limitations, we propose gradient-aligned and imbalance-aware FCIL model (FedGRAIL), a unified FCIL framework that resolves the conflict between local optimization bias and global consistency in dynamic IoT environments. FedGRAIL integrates local training and global aggregation within a structurally aligned learning process, rather than treating them as separate stages. It further introduces a gradient-correction mechanism that coordinates dispersed local optima and stabilizes global optimization via diversity-driven generative replay. This design supports effective retention of minority concepts while respecting the zero-storage constraints of edge agents. Extensive experiments on long-tailed benchmarks show that FedGRAIL substantially improves tail-class accuracy under both independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-IID conditions - achieving a 59% average gain over the strongest baseline, while preserving the competitive accuracy on head classes. These results demonstrate that FedGRAIL provides a storage-efficient, privacy-preserving, and robust solution for continual learning in IoT edge intelligence.
